steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on federated learning for large-scale scene modeling with neural radiance fields. Motivate NeRF-based maps for robotics at large scale, explain the problems with current large-scale NeRF pipelines, and introduce our federated pipeline and its contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- NeRF as maps for robotics, and the move to large-scale environments
- Vision: an earth-scale NeRF map maintained from vehicle and drone data
- Existing large-scale NeRF methods and their three problems
- Our proposal: federated learning for NeRF
- Model aggregation and global pose alignment
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- NeRF for robotics
  - NeRF (cite): scene representation for view synthesis
  - used as maps: vision-based localization, navigation, SLAM (cite)
  - evaluated in small scenes; we expect large-scale use: self-driving cars, delivery drones
  - lift 2D info to 3D, e.g. semantic labels (cite), feature vectors (cite) -> higher-level recognition/understanding
- Vision
  - many vehicles on roads; soon many UAVs / delivery drones
  - system continuously builds and maintains earth-scale NeRF map from vehicle/drone data, life-long learning; use the map
- Existing large-scale NeRF (cite)
  - divide environment into small areas, one NeRF per area; distributed training
  - (i) data collected on server once: high communication cost, large memory for earth-scale data
  - (ii) huge compute to train many models for earth scale
  - (iii) update only per pre-divided area; partial data -> forgetting problem (cite)
- Proposal
  - federated learning pipeline for large-scale NeRF (Fig. 1)
  - FL (cite): data-decentralizing protocol, clients (e.g. mobile devices) collaboratively train, data stays decentralized
  - no data aggregation on server -> less communication and storage
  - uses client resources (millions or more; overall FLOPS much larger than supercomputers)
- Aggregation and alignment
  - tailored aggregation: global model locally updated from client data; avoids forgetting, better maintainability
  - cache local model outputs as 3D voxel grid; aggregate cached representation using client pose in global coordinate
  - outputs beyond locally modeled region unaffected
  - global pose alignment before aggregation for sensor-noise pose errors; inspired by NeRF localization (cite)
- Contributions
  - FL pipeline; voxel-grid caching -> local update of global model
  - global pose alignment: minimize difference of RGB and depth images rendered by global and local models
  - evaluation on Mill19 (cite): thousands of HD drone images, over 100,000m 2 near industrial complex

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Neural radiance fields (NeRF) have appeared as a way to represent scenes for view synthesis, and they have been used as maps in many robotics applications like vision-based localization, navigation and SLAM. These studies were evaluated in fairly small-scale scenes, but we think that NeRF-based robotics applications like these will become available to systems that operate in large-scale environments, for example self-driving cars and delivery drones. Also, NeRF can lift any 2D information to 3D (e.g., semantic labels, and feature vectors), so it will help higher-level recognition and understanding of the environment in robotics applications.

Today a lot of vehicles are on the road, and soon there will also be many unmanned aerial vehicles like delivery drones in the sky. In that world, we imagine a system that continuously builds and maintains an earth-scale NeRF-based map from the data collected by vehicles and drones, in a life-long learning way, and that uses the map created and maintained like this.

Recent years have seen studies on large-scale scene modeling with NeRF. These methods split a large-scale environment into many small areas and model the small areas with multiple NeRF models. This pipeline models a large-scale scene efficiently with distributed training, but it has three problems for realizing the system we envision: (i) the existing pipelines have to collect the data on a server first, which means high communication costs to collect the data from the clients and a large memory budget to store the earth-scale data; (ii) these pipelines need huge computational resources to train the large number of models that cover an earth-scale environment; and (iii) to maintain the NeRF-based map they can only update the model of each pre-divided area, and if the training data is only collected in part of the area, the model can suffer from the forgetting problem.

- Proposal
  - federated learning pipeline for large-scale NeRF (Fig. 1)
  - FL: data-decentralizing protocol, clients (e.g. mobile devices) collaboratively train, data stays decentralized
  - no data aggregation on server -> less communication and storage
  - uses client resources (millions or more; overall FLOPS much larger than supercomputers)
- Aggregation and alignment
  - tailored aggregation: global model locally updated from client data; avoids forgetting, better maintainability
  - cache local model outputs as 3D voxel grid; aggregate cached representation using client pose in global coordinate
  - outputs beyond locally modeled region unaffected
  - global pose alignment before aggregation for sensor-noise pose errors; inspired by NeRF localization
- Contributions
  - FL pipeline; voxel-grid caching -> local update of global model
  - global pose alignment: minimize difference of RGB and depth images rendered by global and local models
  - evaluation on Mill19: thousands of HD drone images, over 100,000m 2 near industrial complex

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Neural radiance fields (NeRF) have appeared as a way to represent scenes for view synthesis, and they have been used as maps in many robotics applications like vision-based localization, navigation and SLAM. These studies were evaluated in fairly small-scale scenes, but we think that NeRF-based robotics applications like these will become available to systems that operate in large-scale environments, for example self-driving cars and delivery drones. Also, NeRF can lift any 2D information to 3D (e.g., semantic labels, and feature vectors), so it will help higher-level recognition and understanding of the environment in robotics applications.

Today a lot of vehicles are on the road, and soon there will also be many unmanned aerial vehicles like delivery drones in the sky. In that world, we imagine a system that continuously builds and maintains an earth-scale NeRF-based map from the data collected by vehicles and drones, in a life-long learning way, and that uses the map created and maintained like this.

Recent years have seen studies on large-scale scene modeling with NeRF. These methods split a large-scale environment into many small areas and model the small areas with multiple NeRF models. This pipeline models a large-scale scene efficiently with distributed training, but it has three problems for realizing the system we envision: (i) the existing pipelines have to collect the data on a server first, which means high communication costs to collect the data from the clients and a large memory budget to store the earth-scale data; (ii) these pipelines need huge computational resources to train the large number of models that cover an earth-scale environment; and (iii) to maintain the NeRF-based map they can only update the model of each pre-divided area, and if the training data is only collected in part of the area, the model can suffer from the forgetting problem.

To get a more scalable and maintainable method, we propose a federated learning pipeline for large-scale modeling with NeRF, shown in Fig. 1. Federated learning (FL) is a training protocol that decentralizes data: clients such as mobile devices train a model together while the training data stays decentralized. FL does not need to gather the data collected by clients on the server, so it can reduce the communication cost problem and the data storage problem. FL also reduces the computational resource problem, because it can use the clients' resources (millions or more in our scenario, so their overall FLOPS will be much larger than those of supercomputers).

To train NeRF with federated learning, we tailor the model aggregation pipeline so that the global model can be updated locally based on the client data, which avoids the forgetting problem and makes maintenance better. More specifically, we cache the outputs of each local model as a 3D voxel grid, and the global model is then updated by aggregating the cached representation based on the clients' pose in the global coordinate. With this pipeline, the outputs of the global model outside the region modeled by the local models are not affected. Also, the global pose of the clients is inaccurate because of sensor noise, so we propose a global pose alignment step before the aggregation step to align it, inspired by vision-based localization using NeRF.

Our contributions are as follows:

- We propose a federated learning pipeline for large-scale scene modeling with NeRF. We cache the outputs of each local model as a voxel grid, and this lets us update the global model locally.

- We also propose global pose alignment. The clients' pose in the global coordinate has sensor noise, so before the aggregation step we align the global pose of each client by minimizing the difference between the RGB and depth images rendered by the global and local models.

- We evaluate how effective our training pipeline is on the Mill19 dataset, which has thousands of HD images collected from drone footage over 100,000m 2 of terrain near an industrial complex.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Neural radiance fields (NeRF) [1] have emerged as a scene representation for view synthesis and have been used as maps for many robotics applications, such as vision-based localization, navigation, and SLAM [2,3,4,5,6,7]. Although these studies have been evaluated in relatively small-scale scenes, we believe that such NeRF-based robotics applications will become available to systems operating in large-scale environments, such as self-driving cars and delivery drones. In addition, since NeRF can lift arbitrary 2D information to 3D (e.g., semantic labels [8] and feature vectors [9]), it will facilitate higher-level environmental recognition and understanding in robotics applications.

Nowadays, a large number of vehicles are on the road, and in the near future many unmanned aerial vehicles, such as delivery drones, will be in the sky. In such a world, we envision a system that continuously builds and maintains an earth-scale NeRF-based map using data collected from vehicles and drones in a life-long learning manner, and that leverages the map created and maintained in this way.

Large-scale scene modeling with NeRF has been studied in recent years [10,11]. These methods divide a large-scale environment into many small areas and model them with multiple NeRF models. Although this pipeline efficiently models a large-scale scene through distributed training, it has three problems for realizing our envisioned system: (i) the existing pipelines need to collect data on a server first, which incurs high communication costs to gather data from clients and requires large memory budgets to store the earth-scale data; (ii) these pipelines require tremendously large computational resources to train the many models needed to cover an earth-scale environment; and (iii) they can only update the model of each pre-divided area to maintain the NeRF-based map, and if the training data is collected in only part of the area, the model may suffer from the forgetting problem [3].

To develop a more scalable and maintainable method, we propose a federated learning pipeline for large-scale modeling with NeRF, as depicted in Fig. 1. Federated learning (FL) [12] is a data-decentralizing training protocol that enables clients, such as mobile devices, to collaboratively train a model while keeping the training data decentralized. Since FL does not need to aggregate the data collected by clients on the server, it can alleviate the communication cost and data storage problems. FL also alleviates the computational resource problem because it can leverage the resources of clients (millions or more in our scenario, whose overall FLOPS will be much larger than those of supercomputers).

To train NeRF in a federated manner, we tailor the model aggregation pipeline so that the global model can be locally updated based on the client data, which avoids the forgetting problem and improves maintainability. Specifically, we cache the outputs of each local model as a 3D voxel grid, and the global model is then updated by aggregating the cached representations based on the clients' pose in the global coordinate. This pipeline does not affect the outputs of the global model beyond the region modeled by the local models. In addition, to align the global pose of clients, which is inaccurate due to sensor noise, we propose a global pose alignment step before aggregation, inspired by vision-based localization using NeRF [2,7,13].

Our contributions are summarized below:

- We propose a federated learning pipeline for large-scale scene modeling with NeRF. By caching the outputs of each local model as a voxel grid, we realize local updates of the global model.

- We also propose global pose alignment. To alleviate the sensor noise in the clients' pose in the global coordinate, we align the global pose of each client before aggregation by minimizing the difference between the RGB and depth images rendered by the global and local models.

- We assess the effectiveness of our training pipeline on the Mill19 dataset [11], which contains thousands of HD images collected from drone footage over 100,000m 2 of terrain near an industrial complex.

References:
